items.title: SOXL: Leveraged Semis Risky as Volatility Rises
items.source_summary: A SeekingAlpha article argues that SOXL, a leveraged semiconductor ETF, presents elevated risk in a rising volatility environment. No specific metrics, thresholds, or supporting data are provided in the content snippet.
items.sofar_gap_analysis: SOFAR's gex-calculator.py and vol-regime.py do not account for leveraged ETF-specific volatility decay or beta-slippage dynamics. Rising volatility disproportionately erodes leveraged ETF NAV due to daily rebalancing, a factor not captured in standard GEX or vol-regime signals. Additionally, ai-synthesis.py lacks sector-level institutional positioning data (e.g., semiconductor sector ETF flows) that would contextualize SOXL risk.

proposed_change.change_description: In vol-regime.py, add a leveraged-ETF decay risk flag that triggers when realized vol exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 30-day RVol > 30), annotating output with expected daily NAV erosion estimate. In ai-synthesis.py, integrate sector ETF flow data (e.g., SOXX/SMH net flows) as a proxy for institutional semiconductor positioning.

items.evidence_basis: Title-only snippet with no quantitative data or author credentials provided.
items.credibility_basis: No author identified, no data or metrics visible in snippet, SeekingAlpha is user-generated content.

items.title: Long-Horizon Anomaly Strategies Tested on Real Estate Sector
items.source_summary: Quantpedia's study tests anomaly-based trading strategies — including moving average trend-following and momentum (rate of change) — applied to the Fama-French 48-industry real estate portfolio (RlEst) using monthly data from July 1926 to December 2025. It evaluates whether these strategies generate superior risk-adjusted returns versus both the standalone real estate index and the broader Fama-French 12-industry market portfolio.
items.sofar_gap_analysis: SOFAR's vol-regime.py and backcheck-score.py both lack sector-specific anomaly weighting and regime-conditioned strategy evaluation. The study's use of Fama-French industry classification to isolate sector behavior maps directly to the absence of sector-conditional regime logic in vol-regime.py. Additionally, backcheck-score.py has no mechanism to evaluate strategy accuracy conditional on sector membership, momentum regime, or trend state — all of which this study operationalizes. The research scrapers also do not ingest Fama-French portfolio return data, which could serve as a systematic regime or factor signal source.

proposed_change.change_description: 1) In backcheck-score.py, add sector-conditional accuracy buckets so prediction performance is tracked separately by GICS or Fama-French sector classification, enabling calibration of signals within real estate and other sectors. 2) In vol-regime.py, add a momentum/trend-state field derived from a configurable moving average crossover on sector ETFs (e.g., XLRE for real estate), classifying the sector as 'trend-up', 'trend-down', or 'neutral' to weight signals accordingly. 3) Add a Fama-French industry return scraper (data available free from Ken French's library) to pull monthly factor and industry portfolio returns as a systematic macro/sector backdrop signal for ai-synthesis.py.

items.evidence_basis: Quantpedia is a credible quantitative research aggregator; the study uses a nearly 100-year dataset with defined methodology (Fama-French classification, moving averages, momentum). Content is partially truncated so full results are not visible, limiting strength to medium.
items.credibility_basis: Quantpedia publishes peer-reviewed and academically grounded research; Fama-French data is a well-established academic standard; near-century dataset adds robustness.
